description: We’re a full team of enthusiastic university students combining Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, and Telecommunications Engineering. We focus on AI, data processing, and building working prototypes from real NASA data.
summary:
We developed TERRA-SENTINEL X, an interactive web platform that turns NASA-ISRO NISAR radar data into flood-change evidence anyone can inspect. Users slide between Before and After radar images, reveal candidate change areas on a map, open an Evidence Card showing before, after and change values in dB with a plain-language reason, and check Smart Doubt, which shows whether each result holds when detection thresholds change.

For the January 2026 Limpopo River flood near Chókwè, Mozambique, we compare two NISAR L2 GCOV acquisitions taken 12 days apart on the same track and frame. Our pipeline flags areas where both HH and HV radar return dropped sharply, a typical sign of new surface water, and maps 180 candidate areas. Running the same method on two pre-flood dates produced 28 times less change, showing the signal is well above background noise.

This matters because floods often happen under cloud, when optical satellites cannot see the ground. Radar sees through clouds, but raw backscatter is hard to interpret. TERRA-SENTINEL X makes it transparent: it shows why each area was flagged and how robust it is, so responders can question and verify results instead of trusting a black-box map.
details:
What it does and how it works

TERRA-SENTINEL X detects and explains flood-related change using NASA-ISRO NISAR radar, focused on the January 2026 Limpopo River flood near Chókwè, Mozambique. We compare two NISAR L2 GCOV acquisitions taken 12 days apart on the same track and frame, aligned on one 60 m grid. Areas where both HH and HV backscatter dropped sharply, a typical sign of new surface water, become candidates. Smart Doubt re-runs detection with relaxed, baseline and strict thresholds to show how stable each result is. The website lets users slide between Before and After images, reveal 180 change areas, and open an Evidence Card with before, after and change values in dB and a plain-language reason.

Benefits and impact

Radar works through clouds, day or night, when optical satellites cannot see the ground. Every result is explained and its uncertainty is visible, so responders can question and verify it instead of trusting a black-box map. The workflow can be reused for any new flood NISAR observes.

Results

54 areas are likely flood with low doubt (about 70% of the mapped area). Running the same method on two pre-flood dates produced 28 times less change, showing the signal is well above background noise.

Tools

NISAR L2 GCOV data (ASF, NASA Earthdata), Python (GDAL, rasterio, NumPy, SciPy, Shapely), Leaflet with HTML/CSS/JavaScript, and GitHub Actions and Pages for validation and deployment.

Creativity

An evidence-first design: users compare the radar images, reveal the change, then read the evidence. Smart Doubt turns uncertainty into a feature, and the pre-flood control test lets the method check itself.

Factors we considered

The data is NISAR BETA, so results are described as candidate changes, not confirmed floods. Wet soil and vegetation can also change the radar signal, so we use two polarizations and a doubt score. Six team roles worked in parallel through one shared output format.

Links

Source code, data sources and validation report: https://github.com/4mohammedalqahtani-svg/terra-sentinel-x

Live demo: https://4mohammedalqahtani-svg.github.io/terra-sentinel-x/
dataRefs: NISAR L2 GCOV BETA V1 (NASA-ISRO, ASF DAAC)
projectRefs: Copernicus EMS Rapid Mapping EMSR857 (Mozambique flood)
